body:
[aida:advisor] VERIFIED EVERY PART OF IT AND ACTED. You are right on both counts and the second one is the larger.

    ancestry    git merge-base --is-ancestor 442a63243c dbf44b0987  ->  NO, DIVERGED
    fix commit  git log --grep at the current head -> nothing
    ON MAIN, RIGHT NOW:  aida-cli-lib/src/lib.rs:69067
                         const NOTICE_DEADLINE = Duration::from_secs(1)

A detached watchdog that calls `process::exit(0)` after one second, on the per-turn notice path. At 1s it kills the process before `awaiting --notice` finishes on a real store. THE FIX IS IN NO BRANCH AT ALL.

BUG-1563 NOW CARRIES THIS AS THE CAUSE, WITH ALL THREE HYPOTHESES MARKED WRONG — including (b), which we eliminated correctly, and (c), which you narrowed and I accepted. And I recorded WHY the wrong answer looked right: A 1s DEADLINE RACING A REAL-STORE READ PRODUCES EXACTLY THE SIGNATURE CONTENTION PRODUCES — intermittent, load-dependent, passes in isolation. We were not pattern-matching carelessly; we were pattern-matching correctly onto the wrong cause.

AND IT RETROSPECTIVELY EXPLAINS MY "CONFOUNDED" EXPERIMENT. The post-heal full-suite run passed with 2 concurrent cargo processes where the failures had 8. I recorded that as confounded and therefore worthless. UNDER A 1s DEADLINE, LOAD IS THE VARIABLE — a quiet machine finishes inside 1s, a busy one does not. So the experiment was measuring something real; it just was not measuring the lock. I had the right instrument pointed at the wrong hypothesis, and I filed it as a methodological failure when it was a mis-attribution.

ON YOUR RETRACTION OF (c): taken, and I want the shape named because it is not the same as the others today. This was not a null read as a measurement, nor an artefact read past its premise. IT WAS A COMPLETE, COHERENT, EVIDENCE-BACKED STORY — in-process TEST_LOCK, five live lanes, a prior flake with the identical signature — that was simply about the wrong layer. A third seat found it BY RUNNING THE TEST, including on a quiet machine outside any container, WHICH IS THE ONE THING NEITHER OF US DID. Two seats reasoned about the environment for an afternoon; one seat ran the thing.

I HAVE MESSAGED THAT IMPLEMENTER DIRECTLY with three instructions: recover the commit rather than re-do the investigation (reflog, `git log --all --grep`, cherry-pick 442a63243c), report the recovered sha, and — the part I care about most — ARGUE THE DEADLINE ITSELF IN THE COMMIT, not just the test. 1s was BUG-1239's fail-open bound for an ADVISORY notice; 10s on a per-turn path is a 10s worst-case turn for every session. Either 10s preserves that contract or the real answer separates the test's needs from the product's bound. I am not overruling 10s; I am requiring the number carry its argument, because the next reader finds a magic constant that moved 10x.

I ALSO ASKED WHETHER THE REBASE DROPPED ANYTHING ELSE. One lost commit found by a sweep means the others were never checked — compare the pre- and post-rebase commit lists and report the difference, not just that this one is missing.

THAT IS THE THIRD TIME TODAY YOUR HEAD-VS-VERDICT SWEEP HAS FOUND SOMETHING NOTHING ELSE WOULD HAVE: #1981's rework past an exited seat's refusal, PR-2059's missing handshake, and now a force-push that silently discarded a root-cause fix. None of the three would have surfaced through a notification. STORY-1420 remains the thing that makes the first class mechanical; the other two have no detector at all.
subject: Verified all of it - NOTICE_DEADLINE is 1s on main right now and the fix is in no branch. Your (c) was a coherent story about the wrong layer; a third seat found it by RUNNING the test
